cleanIntro: This guide follows Cimarron's single-action manual for the Model P family, which does not name the Evil Roy, so check your revolver against it. Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it. The book's revolver is a Colt-pattern single action: a fixed cylinder turning on a base pin, one chamber at a time visible through the loading gate, and an ejector rod under the barrel. Cleaning starts with the same motion loading does — hammer to half cock, gate open, cylinder turned a full revolution under your eye — and the one thing to establish before you touch the base pin is which of the book's two frame types yours is, because the pin is released differently on each.

steps.title: Whose book this is
steps.action: This guide follows Cimarron's single-action manual for the Model P family, which does not name the Evil Roy, so check your revolver against it. The book is printed by Uberti, who build these revolvers, and it addresses your gun as a Uberti single action throughout; Cimarron distributes it as the manual for its single actions. Where your revolver differs from what a step describes, stop and go by the gun in your hand, not by this guide.
steps.prose: Every step that follows is the book's general procedure for the family. Nothing has been added for the Evil Roy that the book does not print.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — ABSENT — no revision or edition line is printed — Cover, printed p.1 (the cover's display type extracts with its spaces lost)

steps.title: A fixed cylinder means you check one chamber at a time
steps.action: Understand what you are about to inspect. Nothing on this revolver swings out to show you all six chambers at once — the cylinder is fixed and turns on the base pin, and only the chamber lined up with the loading gate can be seen. That is why every check on this gun is a full revolution of the cylinder, not a glance.
steps.prose: Six chambers, one window. If you did not turn it all the way round, you did not check it.
steps.quote: Unlike modern revolvers, which provide for the entire cylinder to rotate away from the frame exposing all bores or chambers, this single action revolver has a fixed cylinder which rotates around the cylinder base pin.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — ABSENT — no revision or edition line is printed — General Operation and Nomenclature, printed p.4
steps.warn: ALWAYS KEEP AN EMPTY CHAMBER BELOW THE HAMMER DURING TRANSPORTATION OR STORAGE.

steps.title: Unload with the ejector rod — full stroke, every chamber
steps.action: Bring the hammer back to half cock and open the loading gate fully. Push the ejector rod back toward the cylinder to drive the cartridge or case out through the gate, let the rod return, turn the cylinder to the next chamber and repeat. Use the rod's whole travel each time — a short stroke leaves a case half out, where it binds the cylinder.
steps.prose: The cylinder should turn freely with the gate open and the hammer at half cock. If it will not, stop and find out why before forcing it.
steps.quote: You must operate the ejector rod its full length in each chamber to ensure complete cartridge ejection.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — ABSENT — no revision or edition line is printed — Unloading, printed p.11
steps.warn: Move the hammer rearward to the half cock (loading) position and open the loading gate fully.

steps.title: One more full revolution before anything comes apart
steps.action: With the hammer at half cock and the gate open, turn the cylinder slowly through one complete revolution and look into each of the six chambers in turn. Only when all six have been seen empty does cleaning start. This is a separate check from the unloading you just did, and the manual asks for it separately on purpose.
steps.prose: The gun cannot show you all six at once, so the only proof is having looked at each one. Do it under a light.
steps.quote: Before beginning any cleaning or maintenance procedures, MAKE SURE the revolver is unloaded.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — ABSENT — no revision or edition line is printed — Cleaning and Maintenance, printed p.11
steps.warn: Failure to follow this step could lead to SERIOUS INJURY OR DEATH.

steps.title: Gate open, hammer at half cock
steps.action: The cylinder comes out with the gun in the loading state, not at rest. Open the loading gate and bring the hammer rearward to half cock so the cylinder is free to turn.
steps.prose: At half cock the cylinder turns but the hammer is caught. That is the position the book starts this from.
steps.quote: REMOVING THE CYLINDER: To remove the cylinder, follow these steps: 1. Open the loading gate. 2. Move the hammer rearward to the half cock (loading) position.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — ABSENT — no revision or edition line is printed — Removing the Cylinder, printed p.11

steps.title: Base pin release — two different mechanisms, check yours
steps.action: The book covers two frames and they release the base pin differently: on one you loosen a base pin screw, on the other you depress a spring-loaded base pin screw. Look at your revolver and identify which you have before you turn or press anything — the manual covers both because it cannot know which one you own.
steps.prose: Getting this wrong is how a base pin screw gets rounded off. If the screw resists turning, it may be the spring-loaded type and want pressing, not driving.
steps.caution: The step's second half continues on the next line as "spring-loaded base pin screw, so that the cylinder base pin can be removed from the frame by pulling it out in the direction of the muzzle."
steps.quote: 3. Depending on your model, either loosen the cylinder base pin screw or depress the
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — ABSENT — no revision or edition line is printed — Removing the Cylinder, step 3, printed p.11

steps.title: Base pin forward, cylinder out the gate side
steps.action: With the pin released, draw the cylinder base pin all the way forward out of the frame toward the muzzle. Then take the cylinder out sideways through the frame window on the loading gate side.
steps.prose: The cylinder comes out the gate side and no other. The book says the cylinder is hand-fitted, so expect a close fit and never force it in any direction.
steps.caution: The cylinder in your revolver is hand-fitted to its frame with precision, so there likely will be a close fit.
steps.quote: 4. Slide the cylinder base pin all the way out until it is free of the frame. 5. Remove the cylinder toward the loading gate side of the revolver.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — ABSENT — no revision or edition line is printed — Removing the Cylinder, steps 4–5, printed p.11

steps.title: No steel rod on this revolver
steps.action: Pick the rod before the solvent. The book rules out a steel cleaning rod — use wood, aluminium or brass, with a brass bristle brush and patches sized to your caliber. Scrub the barrel bore with a good cleaning solution.
steps.prose: A steel rod is what wears a crown and scores a chamber mouth.
steps.quote: To clean your revolver, use a wood, aluminum or brass cleaning rod (do not use steel), a brass bristle brush, and patches that are correctly sized to the caliber of your revolver.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — ABSENT — no revision or edition line is printed — Cleaning, printed p.11

steps.title: Brush all the way through — never reverse inside the bore
steps.action: Scrub each of the six chambers the same way as the barrel. Push the brush completely through the chamber and out the far end before you pull it back. Reversing direction while the brush is still inside is what breaks bristles off and can wedge the brush.
steps.prose: Then run clean patches through the bore and every chamber until they come out clean. That is the stopping condition, not a stroke count.
steps.quote: Always brush all the way through the bore; never try to reverse directions while the brush is actually in the barrel or chamber.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — ABSENT — no revision or edition line is printed — Cleaning, printed p.11

steps.title: Oil the whole revolver, lightly
steps.action: Once the patches come out clean, oil the whole revolver completely but lightly — frame, base pin, cylinder and barrel. The book's word is lightly: oil that pools in the frame window collects fouling for the next session.
steps.prose: If your revolver has brass furniture, the book adds that the brass will tarnish and that any good brass polish removes it; that is a separate job from oiling the steel.
steps.quote: Thereafter, completely, but lightly, oil the entire revolver.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — ABSENT — no revision or edition line is printed — Cleaning, printed p.11

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The base pin is out, the cylinder is out through the gate side, and the barrel and six chambers are clean. That is the whole strip this manual publishes — the hammer, bolt, hand and springs appear in the parts diagram but no procedure removes any of them. Use only proper ammunition when it goes back into service.
steps.prose: Everything left in the frame is fitted work, and the book gives the owner no procedure for it.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — ABSENT — no revision or edition line is printed — Special Safety Instructions, printed p.3

deepAbsentReason: The book publishes no procedure beyond removing the cylinder and base pin. Its only disassembly section is REMOVING THE CYLINDER (printed p.11, five steps plus reinstallation); there is no procedure anywhere in its 20 pages for the hammer, trigger, bolt, hand, springs, gate catch, ejector assembly or hammer safety bar — they appear in the parts diagram on printed p.2 as identification only. The book states the cylinder is hand-fitted to its frame and must never be forced, and it stops there.

cleaning.name: BARREL BORE
tasks: Wood, aluminium or brass rod only — never steel
Brass bristle brush and correctly sized patches, with a good cleaning solution
Brush all the way through and out; never reverse direction inside the bore
Patches through until they come out clean, then a light oil

cleaning.name: CYLINDER & CHAMBERS
tasks: Scrub each of the six chambers individually with the brush and solution
Patches through every chamber until they come out clean
Wipe the cylinder clean before it goes back in the frame
Do not force the cylinder into the frame from any direction

cleaning.name: FRAME, BASE PIN & GATE
tasks: Wipe fouling from the frame window and the loading gate
Clean and lightly oil the base pin
Check the base pin catch plunger moves freely and returns under its own spring
Light oil over the whole revolver once it is dry

reassembly: Reverse the removal: cylinder in through the loading gate side of the frame, never forced from any direction.
Slide the cylinder base pin back through the frame and the cylinder from the muzzle end.
Make sure the base pin catch snaps back into place as the pin seats.
Test the catch by depressing the plunger — it must move freely and return under its own spring pressure.
Close the loading gate, lower the hammer, and set the revolver down with an empty chamber under the hammer.
fncheck: With the revolver empty, bring the hammer to half cock, open the gate and turn the cylinder a full revolution — it must turn freely and every chamber must be empty. Depress the base pin catch plunger and confirm it moves freely and returns under its own spring. Close the gate. Then set it down with an empty chamber under the hammer.
